title: Intraday Response of the Term Structure to US Macroeconomic Shocks: Evidence from the B3 DI Futures Market
abstract: This paper investigates price adjustment speed, price discovery, and conditional volatility dynamics across the Brazilian interest rate term structure following US macroeconomic announcements (Non-Farm Payroll and CPI). Using 1-minute high-frequency data of Brazilian DI futures contracts traded on B3 across three maturities-short (DI1F29), intermediate (DI1F32), and long (DI1F37)-, we conduct an intraday event study and estimate joint AR(1)-GARCH(1,1)-X models with HAC Newey-West robust standard errors. Empirical findings reveal monotonic term-structure heterogeneity: in the conditional mean equation, the directional impact of exogenous surprises peaks at the short end and decreases monotonically toward the long end (β Pay declines from +0.3884 to +0.2241; β CPI decreases from +0.2874 to +0.1362, both statistically significant). In the conditional variance equation, releases trigger immediate volatility spikes (γ ≈ 0.046 to 0.049), while persistence (α + β) increases with contractual maturity (0.9257 for DI1F29, 0.9635 for DI1F32, and 0.9812 for DI1F37). The findings support the semi-strong form of the Efficient Market Hypothesis and show that international shocks primarily alter short-to-medium-term domestic monetary policy expectations, whereas longer maturities experience prolonged volatility clustering.
